items.Sentence: The WWTF has a design capacity of 5,190 gallons per day (gpd) and consists of two 1,500-gallon septic tanks, an aerated oxidation pond, a settling pond, and a leach field disposal system.
From the septic tanks, wastewater flows by gravity to an aerated oxidation pond and then to a settling pond.
From the septic tanks, wastewater flows by gravity to an aerated oxidation pond and then to a settling pond.

Under current operating and drought conditions, with flow rates well below the design capacity of the WWTF, the evaporation occurring in the two ponds is sufficient for disposal of wastewater, and it has not been necessary to utilize the leach field system for the past few years.
The primary leach field is approximately 20,000 square ft, and consists of five leach lines of 300 ft each (1,500 ft total) with a distribution header.
The small emergency leach field area is located across Duggans Road, to the west and down-gradient from the school.
Septic tank sludge depth is measured annually. Each tank is pumped out as needed, generally every two or three years.
